title: US Data Centers Use as Much Energy as Some Countries
paragraphs: The largest US data centers are collectively using as much energy as some countries, according to a new study.

The largest data centers, which are used mainly to support the development of AI, are known as "hyperscale data centers," or HDCs. And America's fast-growing number of HDCs has led to worries about carbon dioxide emissions.

Researchers in the US and Italy looked at data from 403 HDCs operating in the US between May 2024 and April 2025. They estimated these HDCs' electricity consumption, how that electricity was generated, and the carbon dioxide emissions that would be created as a result.
They estimated that these HDCs consumed 82 terawatt-hours of electricity — which amounts to 1.8% of all the electricity used in the US during the period studied.

The researchers also estimated that around 54% of the electricity used by these HDCs came from fossil fuels, and that they were responsible for the emission of nearly 26 million metric tons of carbon dioxide. That's about the same as the annual carbon emissions of Denmark, a country of 6 million people.

Gianluca Guidi, the lead author of the study, told CBS News that the research team's estimates were actually likely to be low — because since the end of their study period in April 2025, the number of HDCs in the US has more than doubled.
"The industry is growing faster than anyone can track it," Guidi said.

The tens of thousands of computers inside HDCs create lots of heat, and need constant cooling as they run 24 hours a day. Much of the extra energy they need comes from new gas-fired power, which developers sometimes even build on-site rather than opting for renewable power.
But Guidi says there are better ways to power AI. "We've proven we can build AI really fast. Now, let's prove that we can build it right," he said.
